hyd.d.ni: Level the electron starts in (also: drag the open circle on the diagram)
hyd.d.nf: Level the electron ends in (also: drag the arrowhead on the diagram)
hyd.d.series: Mark all lines of one series in the spectrum (faint) with its limit (dashed)
hyd.d.series2: Lower level of the series: Lyman $n = 1$, Balmer $n = 2$, Paschen $n = 3$, Brackett $n = 4$
hyd.d.bohr: Show the Bohr picture with orbit radii $r_n = n^2 a_0$ (wide screens only)
hyd.d.mode: Emission: the atom drops to the lower level and emits a photon; absorption: it absorbs a photon and rises
hyd.t.goal.levels: The energy of the hydrogen atom is quantized: $E_n = -13.6\ \text{eV}/n^2$, approaching 0 (ionization) as $n \to \infty$
hyd.t.goal.photon: A transition between two levels emits or absorbs one photon with $hf = \Delta E$, so each pair of levels gives one spectral line
hyd.t.obs.crowd: The levels crowd together below 0 eV; the magnified inset on the right (dashed box) spreads out the band from $-0.62$ eV to 0 where $n \ge 5$ lie
hyd.t.obs.balmer: Transitions ending on $n = 2$ (Balmer series) are the only ones in the visible: $3 \to 2$ gives red $\text{H}_\alpha$ (656 nm), $4 \to 2$ blue-green $\text{H}_\beta$ (486 nm)
hyd.t.obs.lyman: Transitions to $n = 1$ (Lyman) release at least 10.2 eV: ultraviolet. Transitions to $n \ge 3$ release little energy: infrared
hyd.t.obs.abs: Swap $n_i$ and $n_f$ (or double-tap an end of the arrow): absorption needs a photon of exactly the same wavelength, so the dark absorption line sits where the bright emission line was
hyd.t.obs.bohr: Bohr picture: the orbit radius grows as $n^2$, so $n = 3$ is 9 times farther out than $n = 1$
hyd.s.goal.series: All lines ending on the same lower level form a series (Lyman, Balmer, Paschen, Brackett)
hyd.s.goal.limit: As $n \to \infty$ the lines crowd together towards the series limit $\lambda_\infty = n_\text{low}^2/R$
hyd.s.obs.converge: Press play: each new line is closer to the previous one; the spacing shrinks towards the dashed limit
hyd.s.obs.regions: Lyman lies entirely in the UV (91 to 122 nm), Balmer mostly in the visible (365 to 656 nm), Paschen and Brackett in the IR
hyd.s.obs.abs: Absorption: the same wavelengths appear as dark lines on a continuous spectrum
hyd.assume.axis: Energy diagram: linear in $E$; the right panel magnifies the dashed band near 0 eV. Levels up to $n = 200$ are drawn; labels where there is room, the selected levels always
hyd.assume.pick: Drag either end of the arrow up or down; it snaps to the nearest level ($n \le 10$). Double-tap an end to reverse the transition
hyd.assume.vacuum: Wavelengths are vacuum values. In air they are about 0.03 % shorter: $\text{H}_\alpha$ 656.5 nm in vacuum, 656.3 nm in air (the value tables usually quote)
hyd.assume.reduced: Computed with the hydrogen Rydberg constant $R_\text{H} = R_\infty/(1 + m_e/m_p) = 1.0968 \times 10^{7}\ \text{m}^{-1}$ (reduced mass): $E_1 = -13.598$ eV, rounded to $-13.60$ eV in the formulas
hyd.assume.log: Spectrum strip: logarithmic wavelength axis from 80 nm to 5 µm; a line beyond it shows as a triangle at the end. Ultraviolet and infrared lines are grey and dashed
hyd.assume.vis: Visible band taken as 380 to 750 nm; photon colours are approximate
hyd.assume.bohr: The Bohr orbits are a semiclassical picture; quantum mechanics replaces them with probability clouds whose size also grows as $n^2$
hyd.s.assume.count: The animation shows the first 12 lines of a series; infinitely many more crowd in before the limit
